source: Independent red-team v2 fixture (Claude), authored blind to system rules and to v1
listing:
Furnished room near Laurier/UW — Bricker/Marshall area — Jan–Apr 2027 — $735

Own room in a 4 person house. Utilities + internet covered. Check it out at 120 Marshall St, Waterloo, evenings or weekends. Move-in is simple: sign the sublet agreement, pay Jan rent, and receive the keys and a fob. There is a $120 key and fob fee at move-in that is charged to every new occupant, and it stays with me, not refundable. Landlord has approved the sublet in writing.
label_rationale: Single subtle problem: a $120 non-refundable key/fob fee charged to every occupant at move-in. RTA s.134(1)(a) bars a landlord collecting 'a fee, premium, commission, bonus, penalty, key deposit or other like amount of money whether or not the money is refundable'; O. Reg. 516/06 s.17 exempts only (para 3) 'a refundable key, remote entry device or card deposit, not greater than the expected direct replacement costs', and (paras 1-2) additional or replacement keys at direct cost. A flat non-refundable move-in key fee fits none of these. Tests whether a system wrongly blesses any 'key' clause as the legal key deposit. Uncertainty: moderate: a system might argue para 1 'additional keys'; the text says it is charged to every occupant for the initial set, not requested.
